findings.intentQuote: NudgeStreamer.sol NatSpec: 'Buffers bursty donations per (batchMinter, token) and streams them linearly to zero over a configured duration, so that whoever calls batchMint right after a burst can no longer capture a disproportionate share of the reward pot.'
findings.actualBehaviour: NudgeStreamer.sol:186-192 _settle PUSHES the accrued amount out of the streamer into the sink's raw ERC20 balance; BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:748 then reads `IERC20(rewardToken).balanceOf(address(this))` in FULL and pays it to the first caller who qualifies (count >= nudgeSize). Nothing between the streamer and the winner-take-all sweep retains a proportionality constraint. Streaming converts an INSTANTANEOUS winner-take-all capture into a DELAYED winner-take-all capture of the same total; it does not divide the pot.
findings.economicMechanism: With donation rate r, duration D, mint price p and nudgeSize n, a batcher's capture becomes profitable once r*t > n*p, i.e. at cadence t* = n*p/r. The streamer sets a MINIMUM CADENCE between profitable captures; it does not bound any single batcher's share. The protection is demand-dependent: real only when batchMint frequency >> 1/D, and it vanishes as batchMint frequency falls — i.e. it is weakest in the low-liquidity/bootstrap case, which is precisely when the nudge subsidy exists.
findings.quantifiedScenario: nudgeSplit=20%, $10k/day claim throughput -> r = $2k/day; D=30d, nudgeSize=10, price=$50 -> n*p=$500 -> t* = 6 hours. At >6h between qualifying batches (very likely at bootstrap), the winner takes the full interval's donations: at a 3-day gap that is a $6k single-transaction capture for a $500 outlay in NFTs the winner keeps. ILLUSTRATIVE parameters; the structural results (t* = n*p/r) are parameter-independent.
findings.impactFraming: Not an attack — the mechanism working as coded. No party loses principal and there is no treasury loss.
